resolvedQuestions.question: What process, relay, and client architecture preserves Pi RPC semantics while tolerating mobile disconnects?
Which Pi RPC commands and events map to session lists, streaming chat, tool activity, and approvals?
What state model and reconnection protocol prevent duplicated prompts, lost deltas, or stale approvals?
Which security and network exposure model is safe for a coding agent with workspace tool authority?
How should PWA notifications, background limits, and Claude-style mobile UX be implemented and phased?

keyFindings.summary: Relay owns persistent Pi RPC child and strict-LF demux.
Prompt acceptance differs from agent settlement.
Relay sequences complement Pi contentIndex/toolCallId.
Durable entry cursors exist; session listing is relay-owned.
Reconnect requires replay, reconciliation, and deduplication.
Approvals require extension UI plus policy.
UI uses orthogonal mutation, run, rendering, approval, and reconciliation axes.
Relay envelopes use session stream epoch and event sequence.
Mutation idempotency is independent of RPC request IDs.
Message deltas assemble by contentIndex and terminal message replaces draft.
Tool progress replaces accumulated state and end is terminal.
SessionManager.list stays server-side; clients receive opaque session IDs.
Approval responses are first-response-wins and scoped to principal/session/epoch/payload.
Epoch/window acceptance matrix detects replay duplicates, gaps, eviction, and child replacement.
Committed snapshot barrier fences reconciliation from later transient events.
Foreign entry cursor triggers full entry/cache/leaf replacement.
Relay-only exactly-once cannot close Pi stdin crash window; dispatching recovers indeterminate.
Session switching aborts/disposes outgoing session; isolate active sessions.
Child restart creates a new epoch and invalidates transient state and approvals.
Multi-client approval combines policy authorization with CAS lease and first-decision gate.
Default to tailnet-only Serve; public exposure is an explicit exception.
Separate network/device admission from relay identity and per-action authorization.
Require WSS, exact Origin, SameSite cookie, connection ticket, and live revocation.
Authorize server-owned workspace/session/action tuples and enforce OS containment.
Prevent secret access; redact before replay, fan-out, audit, or push.
Bound queues/rates per principal and reserve a safety-control lane.
Approval extension is pinned privileged TCB code and fails closed.
Dependency failures reduce authority through reject, redact, quarantine, or indeterminate states.
iOS Web Push requires Home Screen app; Android support is capability/release-matrix gated.
Service workers are event-bounded; relay exclusively owns Pi/WSS lifecycle.
Push derives from committed settlement/approval/indeterminate transitions and deduplicates.
Push is metadata-only; approval requires foreground reauthentication and current-state validation.
Onboarding stages tailnet, relay identity, install, then user-gesture notification consent.
Offline is bounded redacted read-only state with mutations disabled.
MVP has explicit session, thread/tool, approval, and connection surfaces with accessibility invariants.
Product phases by verified authority/lifecycle, not visual parity.
Core topology holds when ingress, relay, RPC, approval, and OS isolation are explicit seams.
Standard confirm has no signed capability; freeze canonical args and gate as final handler/wrapper.
Serve identity headers bootstrap authentication only; WSS propagation and bypass remain runtime gates.
Replay/barrier/idempotency remains relay-inferred and needs real fault testing.
Redaction precedes sequenced persistence and covers every derived/remote representation.
Session navigation uses isolated active children or exclusive idle switching.
Platform and WCAG docs narrow targets, but device and assistive-tech evidence remains open.

every extension UI request as approval
transient reducer across epoch or gap

P0: deployment identity, backend-bypass, authorization, and OS containment
P1: raw-data leakage through a redaction bypass
P1: private-origin mobile push and stale-approval races
P1: accessibility under streaming and reconciliation
